q: 66. The cut or broken portion of brick is called
explain: A brick bat is a piece of brick with one or more ends cut off, usually across the width.

q: 67. The part of brick cut from a whole brick to maintain the bond in such a way that its one long face remains uncut is known as
explain: A closer is a portion of a brick used to close the bond at the end of a course, such as a queen closer or king closer.

q: 68. The portion of brick obtained by cutting a brick lengthwise into two directions is known as
explain: A queen closer is made by cutting a brick lengthwise into two equal halves, often used next to a quoin header.

q: 69. The slenderness ratio for masonry walls should not be more
explain: For safety against buckling, masonry codes typically limit the slenderness ratio (height to thickness) to 20 for cement mortar walls.

q: 70. Types of plaster generally used for ceiling is
explain: A richer mix like 1:3 is used for ceilings to ensure better adhesion and to resist gravity more effectively than leaner mixes.

q: 71. In brick masonry, the bond produced by laying alternate headers and stretchers in each course is known as
explain: Flemish bond consists of alternate headers and stretchers in every course.

q: 72. In Nepal, the generally used method of bond in masonry wall of brickwork is
explain: English bond is widely preferred for its superior strength, consisting of alternate courses of headers and stretchers.

q: 73. The type of bond provided in brick masonry for carrying heavy loads
explain: English bond is considered the strongest bond in brick masonry and is used for structures subjected to heavy loads.

q: 74. The stretcher bond in brick masonry can be used only when the wall is of
explain: Stretcher bond lacks internal ties across the wall thickness, making it suitable only for partition walls (half-brick thick).

q: 75. In ordinary residential/public buildings, the D.P.C. is provided at
explain: The Damp Proof Course (DPC) is standardly placed at the plinth level to prevent capillary moisture from rising into the walls.

q: 76. D. P. C. stands for
explain: DPC stands for Damp Proof Course, a barrier of impervious material applied to prevent moisture ingress.

q: 77. The method of damp proofing in which a layer of water repellent substance is provided, between the source of dampness and part of structure, adjacent to it is known as
explain: Membrane damp proofing involves applying a water-repellent layer or sheet (like bitumen) between the source of moisture and the building.

q: 78. The DPC is provided in building in the form of
explain: DPC can be applied horizontally (at floor/plinth levels) or vertically (on basement walls) to block moisture from different directions.

q: 79. Generally DPC is provided at
explain: While vertical DPC exists, the most common application in general building construction is a horizontal layer at the plinth.

q: 80. The D. P. C. is provided at
options: just below the ground floor level
below the top most floor level
explain: DPC is usually placed at the plinth level, which is just below the ground floor level, to intercept moisture rising from the foundation.

q: 81. The process of hardening the concrete by keeping its surface moist is known
explain: Curing is the maintenance of moisture and temperature conditions to allow concrete to develop its intended strength and durability.

q: 82. Slump used for beam & slab for RCC.
explain: Beams and slabs require medium workability (50-100mm slump) to ensure the concrete flows around dense reinforcement.

q: 83. Slump test in used for
explain: The slump test is a field test used to measure the consistency and workability of fresh concrete.

q: 84. Which of the following is not a tool used in laying brick wall
explain: An auger is a drilling tool used for soil or wood; it is not used in bricklaying like a trowel or plumb bob.

q: 85. Workability of concrete for a given water content is good if aggregates used are
explain: Rounded aggregates have a lower surface area and less friction, which improves the workability of the concrete mix.

q: 86. Which type of foundation is likely to be adopted for a 3 storey RCC framed building?
explain: For a standard 3-story framed building with good soil, isolated footings under each column are the most common and economical choice.

q: 87. Permissible compressive strength of M 15 concrete grade is
explain: The '15' in M15 refers to its characteristic compressive strength of 15 N/mm², which is equivalent to 150 kg/cm².

q: 88. Water cement ratio for M10 concretes should be
explain: M10 is a lean concrete mix; a water-cement ratio of 0.65 is typically used to ensure enough hydration for this grade.

q: 89. The ratio of various ingredients (cement: sand: aggregates) in concrete of grade M20 is
explain: The standard nominal mix for M20 concrete is 1 part cement, 1.5 parts sand, and 3 parts coarse aggregate (1:1.5:3).

q: 90. The process of mixing, transporting, placing and compacting concrete using ordinary portland cement should not take more than
explain: The initial setting time of OPC is about 30 minutes; all operations should be completed before this to prevent loss of workability.

q: 91. The mortar in which both cement and lime are used as binding materials, is called
explain: Gauged mortar is a combination of cement and lime, offering the strength of cement with the workability of lime.

q: 92. The apex line of a sloping roof is called
explain: The ridge is the horizontal peak where two sloped roof planes meet.

q: 93. Minimum width of load bearing wall should be
explain: A standard load-bearing brick wall is usually at least one full brick thick (roughly 230mm including plaster).

q: 94. The maximum percentage of chemical ingredient of cement is that of
explain: Lime (Calcium Oxide) makes up 60-67% of Portland cement, being its primary constituent.

q: 95. A plate load test is useful to determine
explain: The plate load test provides data on both the ultimate bearing capacity of the soil and the anticipated settlement under load.

q: 96. The height of slump cone is
explain: The standard dimensions for a slump cone are 30 cm height, 20 cm bottom diameter, and 10 cm top diameter.

q: 97. The unit weight of RCC is taken as
explain: Reinforced Cement Concrete (RCC) has a standard density of 2500 kg/m³, which equals 2.5 t/m³.

q: 98. The maximum thickness of door shutters provided in door in
explain: Standard commercial and residential door shutters are typically manufactured in thicknesses around 38 mm.

q: 99. Small window is which shutters are allowed to swing around pivots fixed to the window frame
explain: A pivoted window has a sash that rotates on horizontal or vertical pivots located at the center of the frame.

q: 100. Door type without importance
explain: Battened and ledged doors are the simplest and cheapest type, used for low-importance applications like sheds or toilets.

q: 101. The vertical member fixed between steps and handrail is known as
explain: Balusters are the vertical posts that support the handrail of a staircase.

q: 102. The member laid horizontally to support common rafters and which transmits the loads to the trusses or wall are
explain: Purlins are horizontal beams that run parallel to the ridge to support the common rafters.

q: 103. The maximum total settlement for raft foundation on clayey soils is usually limited to
explain: For clayey soils, raft foundations are generally designed to limit total settlement to 65-100 mm.

q: 104. The maximum total settlement for raft foundation on sand is usually limited to
explain: Settlement in sand occurs more rapidly and is typically capped at 40-65 mm for raft foundations.

q: 105. The maximum differential settlement in case of foundation on clayey soils is usually limited to
explain: To prevent structural damage in clay, differential settlement (difference in settlement between two points) is limited to 40 mm.

q: 106. The maximum differential settlement, in case of foundation on sandy soils is usually limited to
explain: In sandy soils, the allowable differential settlement is stricter, usually limited to 25 mm.

q: 107. The maximum total settlement for isolated foundation on clayey soils should be limited to
explain: Isolated footings on clay are typically permitted a total settlement of up to 65 mm.

q: 108. The minimum thickness of a wall in stone masonry cannot be less than
explain: Because stone units are large and irregular, stone masonry walls must have a minimum thickness (usually 35-40 cm) to ensure stability.

q: 109. In public buildings the minimum tread width of stair case should be
explain: For safety and ease of use in public spaces, codes require a minimum tread width of 30 cm.

q: 110. The minimum width of a stair in a residential building is
explain: Building codes generally specify a minimum width of 80 cm to 90 cm for residential stairs to allow for safe passage and the movement of furniture.

q: 111. Raft foundation are generally preferred to when the area required for individual footing is more than
explain: When individual footings cover more than 50% of the building area, a continuous raft (mat) becomes more economical and better at preventing differential settlement.

q: 112. In public buildings the maximum riser is limited to
explain: Public buildings require easier ascent for diverse users; therefore, the riser is restricted to 15 cm, whereas residential buildings may allow up to 19 cm.

q: 113. The joints provided in wooden floor are
explain: Tongue and groove joints are standard for flooring because they allow for expansion/contraction while maintaining a flush, interlocking surface.

q: 114. The highest point of an arch is called
explain: The crown is the highest point of the arch, where the keystone is typically located.

q: 115. Pile foundation is generally provided if soil is
explain: Piles are deep foundations used when surface soil is weak, highly compressible, or waterlogged, transferring the load to deeper, more stable strata.

q: 116. Safe bearing capacity of Black cotton soil varies from
explain: Black cotton soil is notoriously unstable due to high swelling and shrinkage; its safe bearing capacity is very low, typically 5 to 7.5 t/m².

q: 117. The process of finding out the soil strata below ground level is known as
explain: Subsoil exploration involves boring and sampling to determine the engineering properties and layers of the soil before construction.

q: 118. A temporary rigid structure having platform to enable masons to work at different stages of a building is known as
explain: Scaffolding is the temporary framework used to support workers and materials during the construction or repair of a building.

q: 119. The arrangement of supporting an existing structure by providing supports underneath is known as
explain: Underpinning is the method used to strengthen or deepen the foundation of an existing building or structure.

q: 120. Temporary structure constructed in a river for excluding water from a given site to enable the building operation to be performed on dry surface is called
explain: A cofferdam is a watertight enclosure pumped dry to allow construction work (like bridge piers) below the waterline.

q: 121. A junction at which two walls meet at an angle other than 90° is called
explain: A squint junction occurs when walls meet at an acute or obtuse angle, requiring special 'squint' bricks.

q: 122. A horizontal layer of brick laid in mortar is known as
explain: In masonry, a 'course' refers to a single continuous horizontal layer of units such as bricks or stones.

q: 123. For a building one side of the busy street where the ordinary scaffolding will obstruct the traffic on the road, the type of scaffolding provided is
explain: Needle scaffolding (cantilever scaffolding) is supported by 'needles' passing through the wall, keeping the ground level clear for traffic.

q: 124. A brick which is cut in such a way that the width of its one end is half that is a full brick is called
explain: A king closer is created by cutting off a triangular corner so that one header end and one stretcher end are half-width.

q: 125. The most commonly used flooring in residential and public buildings is
explain: Cement concrete flooring is the most common due to its durability, ease of construction, and economy.

q: 126. Flooring used in both rooms and kitchens of posh residential building is
explain: Marble flooring is preferred in high-end (posh) residences for its aesthetic appeal and luxury status.

q: 127. The bearing of the lintel should be
explain: The minimum bearing (overlap on the wall) for a lintel is usually 10 cm, the height of the lintel, or 1/12th of the span—whichever is greatest.

q: 128. The function of cleats in a roof truss is
options: to prevent the purlins from tilting
explain: Cleats are short angle pieces fixed to the principal rafter to prevent the purlins from sliding or tilting.

q: 129. The term string is used for
options: outer projecting edge of a tread
a sloping member which supports the steps in a stair
a vertical member between two treads
explain: A string (or stringer) is the sloping wooden or steel member that supports the treads and risers of a staircase.

q: 130. The vertical posts placed at the top and bottom ends of a flight supporting the hand rail are known as
explain: Newel posts are the heavy vertical posts at the start, end, or turns of a handrail system.
